We chose Wak Wak based on the numerous positive reviews and were not disappointed. As a tourist, I'm always cautious about restaurant selections, but this experience exceeded my expectations.
We ordered the Triple Magical Layers in medium, along with extra chicken tenders and fries to sample a variety of options. As Germans, we appreciate good sauces, so we tried all they offered. The quality of the food was impressive—especially considering that this isn't always the case in Egypt—and the portion sizes were generous. Each sauce was unique and unlike anything I've encountered before.
The chicken tenders were made from fresh chicken breasts, not processed meat, and they were juicy on the inside with a perfect crunch on the outside. The spices used on both the chicken and fries were exceptional; I even inquired about purchasing some of the fry seasoning.
The Triple Magical Layers is a standout dish, combining fries, chicken tenders, pasta, and a delicious cheese sauce. The pasta was cooked just right, not too soft. This dish is a must-try; I've never encountered anything like it, even in the US.
We dined in the restaurant, which was clean and beautifully decorated, complete with a window to observe the kitchen. As someone who studied food hygiene and nutrition, I was keen to see the preparation process. I was pleased to find the kitchen spotless, with everything prepared fresh—a refreshing experience given my previous encounters in Egypt.
I loved the food so much that I ordered it again on the day of my departure. I truly hope to return to Alexandria and enjoy WakWak again.

A brief about my visit today 05-12-2025

We went to The Hub Cafe & Restaurant in Alexandria as a group of friends on the evening of 25 July 2024, at around 11 PM. Unfortunately, our experience there was extremely disappointing.

Upon arrival, we ordered a variety of items including juice, cheesecake, and waffles. To our dismay, the drinks were served after an hour and a half, and they were quite average in quality. This significant delay was frustrating, so we asked the waiters to explain the cause of the holdup and urged them to expedite our order.

Regrettably, the cheesecake and waffles took even longer to arrive. The cheesecake was just okay, but the waffles were absolutely terrible. They were not prepared properly, and some of the sauces, especially the pistachio sauce, were particularly bad.

We decided to speak with the manager about our experience, but the waiters kept procrastinating and arguing that the place was full of customers. While it was true that the restaurant was busy, the delays at our table were longer than those experienced by people who arrived after us.

Eventually, the manager came to our table and apologized for the delay. We asked him to taste the waffle, and he took one of the dishes. After some time, he returned and admitted that the waffle was not cooked properly. He apologized again and took the remaining dishes, promising to have them cooked again properly.

However, it was already very late by then, so we asked for the check. As an apology, they applied a 10% discount to our bill. We didn’t wait for the new waffles to be prepared and left feeling extremely disappointed.

Overall, it was a very bad experience and a waste of time. I deeply regret not checking the reviews of this place before deciding to dine there.

A century-old Alexandrian dessert shop, serving a variety of harissa to tourists and locals alike.

Ordered: Hazelnut Harissa with cream on top

Ever since 1909, this little parlor has maintained its humble facade and mom-and-pop-shop-like service, well, at least in their primary branch. Situated near the famed El Raml terminus, it is hard to miss this local favourite, and that in itself is a blessing if you ask me.

Their harissa is what I would call the golden standard: crispy(but not hard) on the outside, soft and moist(but not chewy) on the inside. The dessert melts in your mouth with a perfect balance of syrupy sweetness and butter richness, which, when paired with the earthy notes of hazelnut, gives an almost chocolatey essence to the petit delight.

I would like to add that it is almost always worth it to add the extra cream as a topping. The fresh, perfectly rolled finger of buttery goodness only adds to the overall experience.

Given their heritage, quality, and location, it would be a shame to miss Al Halabi on your Alexandria visit.

I had a very pleasant stay at the hotel. The place is beautiful, very clean, and the sea view was absolutely amazing. The atmosphere was calm and relaxing, which made our stay even more enjoyable.

However, I would like to share a few comments for improvement:

I would appreciate clarification about the sanitization process of the bracelets provided to guests, as they are reused and this was a bit concerning from a hygiene perspective.

The bathroom does not have proper ventilation or an exhaust fan. With the use of hot water, steam accumulates heavily. I personally felt unwell due to the steam, and the bathroom floor becomes completely wet.

When the garden irrigation is in progress, water surrounds the area from multiple sides, which makes it difficult to leave the room comfortably during that time.

Overall, the stay was very good, and with a little more attention to these points, the guest experience would be even better. Thank you for the hospitality, and I hope to visit again.

Fathallah Group started its business in 1948 under the name of Mossad Fathallah & Bros. by selling spices, grains, coffee, and tea by wholsale in the markets of El-Manshia in Alexandria, and then such business was developed to wholesale all over the Republic of Egypt, and expanded to include canned foods, detergents and food of all kinds. Then it began importing from abroad to become one of the largest importers of spices and tea in the Middle East,  and also one of the largest importers, traders and distributors of foods and canned foods in Egypt.
In order to complete the business development, establishing the first chain store selling goods directly to consumers at the wholesale price along with the import and basic trade.

The beginning came with the second generation of the family by opening the first branch of Fathallah Gomla Market and currently:
TREE Chain Stores provides the largest collection and variety of Egyptian industry for men wear, with high quality cotton materials, in the framework of fashion for all ages at competitive prices in addition to shoes, socks, travel bags and accessories, and for the first time in Egypt, TREE Perfumes & Cosmetics chain Stores providing original perfumes and make-up to the consumer at the lowest wholesale price in Egypt,  in operation with the certified agencies accredited in this field in order to ensure the absence of non-original products.

The hotel itself was below expectations: poor food quality, unclean rooms, and very basic facilities. When participants complained, no effective action was taken.

The advertised program was also changed without prior notice, the promised dolphin yacht trip became a general coral reef trip instead, and we only had two yoga sessions instead of the six included in the plan.

I’ve been a member at Gold’s Gym Alexandria for over a month time, but unfortunately, my experience has been getting worse over the month. At first, things seemed promising – they made several impressive claims during the membership sign-up process. However, those promises haven’t been met, and the quality of service has declined noticeably.

Parking Issues
One major frustration is the parking situation. Unless you’re willing to pay 15 EGP each day, finding a spot can be a nightmare. This adds up to around 5,000 EGP a year – nearly 50% of the membership fee itself, which feels unreasonable and poorly managed.

Security Concerns
On top of that, while I was in the gym, my car’s logo was stolen. This lack of security leaves me concerned about the safety of my property every time I visit.

Unmet Membership Promises
When I signed up, I was told that I’d receive a 13-month membership, with an additional month for referring someone. Despite referring a friend, I only received 12 months. This overpromising and under-delivering has been disappointing and makes me feel like my trust in them was misplaced.

Facilities Maintenance
The spa area is in dire need of attention, and maintenance standards seem low across the gym. The sauna room door doesn’t seal properly, and members are left to bring a plastic bottle instead of having a wooden bucket for water. Additionally, the treadmills seem to have a circuit issue; whenever my hands start to sweat, I feel a shock. I’ve reported these problems multiple times, but no action has been taken, which shows a lack of accountability from the staff.

Final Recommendation
In short, the experience has been underwhelming and frustrating. It’s clear that the focus here is more on money than on maintaining a quality environment for members. I wouldn’t recommend this gym if you’re looking for a professional, well-maintained space.

An Unforgettable Authentic Seafood Experience in Alexandria!

Rating: ★★★★★

Our visit to Abdo Farag Seafood Restaurant  on the Mediterranean beach in Bahary, Alexandria was nothing short of spectacular and perfectly captured the essence of a classic Alexandrian fish meal. From the incredibly fresh catch to the warm and genuine service, every element exceeded our expectations.

You are greeted by a fantastic spread of the day's fresh catch. The process is engaging: you get to select your own fish, shellfish, and prawns, which are then weighed right in front of you before you decide how you'd like each item cooked—whether grilled, pan-fried, or in a soup. This transparency is wonderful and ensures you get exactly what you want.

Here’s what makes this restaurant stand out:

Exceptional Food Quality: The seafood is exceptionally fresh. We tried the grilled seabass and it was perfectly cooked, flaky, and flavorful. The butter prawns were also a highlight—fresh, succulent, and delicious. Do not miss the seafood crème soup; it is rich, flavorful, and brimming with treasures from the sea. The fried fish and shrimp soup also come highly recommended.

Fair and Transparent Value: While some visitors note the prices can be on the higher side, many others find them reasonable and a fair value for the outstanding quality and portion sizes. The fact that they clearly weigh the seafood in front of you and that many tourists report not being overcharged is a significant plus.

Welcoming and Attentive Service: The staff, including the hospitable Mr. Farag, are friendly and work hard to make you feel welcome. Despite a potential language barrier, they are accommodating and willing to help. The service is often described as outstanding, contributing greatly to the positive experience.

Authentic Local Atmosphere: The restaurant boasts a genuine, homey atmosphere that is popular among both tourists and locals. It provides that classic, bustling seafood market feel that makes dining here a real experience.

Abdo Farag Fish Restaurant is a must-visit seafood haven in Alexandria. It delivers on every front: breathtaking freshness, delicious flavors, fair value, and generous hospitality. We left already planning our next visit and cannot recommend it highly enough!

Title: A Sunlit Nostalgic Getaway at Stanley Beach!

Review:

My recent visit to Stanley Beach in Alexandria was nothing short of spectacular. As someone hailing from New York, I sought a unique spot far from the typical tourist trails, and Stanley Beach did not disappoint. Despite its smaller size, the beach's historic charm and the grandeur of the iconic Stanley Bridge created a perfect backdrop for a day under the Egyptian sun.

I spent my time soaking up the sunshine and enjoying the refreshing breeze without dipping into the water. The sight of waves breaking against the shore and the scenic views around the Stanley neighborhood were mesmerizing. What made the experience even more enjoyable was the tranquility of the beach, allowing me to fully appreciate the beauty of the moment and the sounds of nature.

For anyone visiting Alexandria, Stanley Beach offers a slice of the city's cosmopolitan past, wrapped in the sunlit tranquility of today. Whether planning to swim or sit back and relax like I did, this beach is a must-visit. Remember, it's more about the atmosphere and the views than the amenities, so come prepared for a laid-back, scenic experience.

Koshary El Tahrir, one of Egypt's most renowned eateries specializing in koshary, a traditional Egyptian street food. Koshary El Tahrir is celebrated for its consistent quality, flavorful recipes, and hygienic preparation, making it a go-to spot for locals and tourists alike.

The restaurant chain offers a simple yet satisfying menu centered around koshary, a mix of rice, lentils, pasta, chickpeas, and fried onions, topped with a tangy tomato sauce and optional garlic vinegar or spicy chili sauce. Known for quick service and generous portions, Koshary El Tahrir caters to a wide range of customers, from casual diners to those seeking an authentic Egyptian culinary experience.

The branch on the map likely provides a clean, comfortable dining area, takeaway options, and affordable prices, embodying the chain's reputation for accessibility and quality. It’s a must-try for anyone exploring Egypt's vibrant food culture.

Service has also declined—fewer items provided with the meal, and I had to ask for basic things like a spoon and wipes,There was also an order mix-up when I took food to go. The open kitchen didn’t look as clean as before while the prices keep going up.

Overall, it used to be excellent, but the quality has clearly declined and it feels like just another average fast food place now.

A hidden treasure in the heart of Alexandria . From the moment I stepped in, I knew this place was something special. The ambience is stunning, warm, laid-back, and effortlessly cool. It’s one of those rare spots where time slows down and everything just feels right. I actually took off my noise-canceling AirPods, which I never do, just to soak in the energy, the soft background music, and the subtle buzz of conversation. That alone says everything.

It’s the ideal place to sip coffee, catch up with a friend, or zone in and get work done. They even have fast, reliable WiFi—something I haven’t found to be common in Egypt, and it makes a huge difference.

Syrian cuisine includes the cooking traditions and practices of modern Syria (as opposed to Greater Syria), merging the habits of people who settled in Syria throughout its history.

It is heavily influenced by Ottoman Turkish and Arab cuisine.

Syrian cuisine mainly uses eggplant, zucchini, garlic, meat (mostly from lamb and sheep), sesame seeds, rice, chickpeas, fava beans, lentils, cabbage, cauliflower, vine leaves, pickled turnips, cucumbers, tomatoes, olive oil, lemon juice, mint, pistachios, honey and fruits.

At the beginning of the 21st century, selections of appetizers known as mezze are customarily served along with Arabic bread before the Syrian meal's main course, which is followed by coffee, with sweet confections or fruits at will. Many recipes date from at least the 13th century.[1]

Ordered: Snickers Cake Bar

Alright, I usually like to begin by talking about atmosphere, but the seating area in this branch was being renovated, and thus, I will go right into the food.

Let me begin by saying I loved the cake, but for a very unexpected reason.

You see, the guy there had recommended the Snickers cake, which I, despite disliking traditional “snickers-inspired” pastry, decided to purchase to honor the man’s recommendation.

Funnily enough, to its advantage, the cake had very little to do with a Snickers. Most Snickers cakes use an obnoxious amount of peanuts or peanut butter, which, when mixed with caramel, can be extremely overwhelming. This cake rarely uses any peanuts and leans more hazelnutty in its cream filling, which I preferred.

It did, however, use caramel, which would have made this cake far too sweet, if it wasn't for the balancing tang of some form of red fruit jam between the chocolate sponge cake layers (btw, great sponge cake). I mean, credit where it's due, the place called Genoise makes pretty damn good genoise.

Also, don’t let the size fool you; this boy was dense. It was like a robust black forest cake with a hard chocolate casing, which was a welcome twist on one of my favourite kinds of cake.

I really enjoyed this dessert, and I look forward to trying more of their stuff. Give them a try if you are getting a sugar craving in the neighbourhood!

Their croissants are simply divine – buttery, flaky, and freshly baked to perfection. Paired with their rich, aromatic coffee, it felt like a perfect Parisian breakfast without leaving Egypt. The selection of desserts is also incredibly impressive – elegant, beautifully presented, and full of flavor.

The atmosphere is cozy yet upscale, with a charming French aesthetic that makes it ideal for a quiet morning coffee or an indulgent afternoon treat. Every detail, from the service to the ambiance, reflects quality and care.

Le Gout Parisien is not just a café – it’s an experience. Highly recommended for anyone looking to treat themselves to a little luxury and unforgettable flavors.

Alexandrian Boulangerie and Patisserie operating in the Manshia Area near Ahmed Oraby Square.

Ordered: Nutella Croissant

Practically everyone who lives in this city knows about this bakery; they’ve garnered regional fame so powerful it transcends generations. And so, I did know about this place, and I have had their bakeries before (I’ve even had some of their croissants), but that didn’t prepare me for this immaculate work of artisanal baked delight.

The outer crust is crispy and breaks with a subtle, dopamine-inducing, brittle flakiness. Its dough is soft, airy, and buttery, creating the signature fluffiness coveted by all who wish to capture the essence of true Croissant Francais. The filling is generous, creamy, and bursting with the rich profile of sweet roasted hazelnuts.

Decadent, delightful, delicious. This is a croissant that captures the golden ratio, making it worthy of standing amongst la creme de la creme.

If only it weren’t for the leaky hole in the bottom, where the filling had been pumped into the pastry, then it would be perfect.

I advise you to wear a glove or serve it on a plate. This way, you can enjoy the croissant without adjusting it repeatedly to make sure your clothes aren't drenched in Nutella.

All things considered, this croissant is a must-try if you visit the city of Alexandria.

I stopped by بنtree for coffee since it’s close by and decided to give it a try. They have good eclairs, but nothing savory for breakfast—just coffee and a few dessert options, which isn’t ideal in the morning. That said, the eclair I tried was pretty good, and the place does have its own unique character.

One thing I really appreciated was how knowledgeable the baristas are. They seem to know so much about coffee and the different varieties they serve, and they’re super informative if you ask. I also shared my feedback about the overall experience, and they were very welcoming and open to it, which left a positive impression.

That said, the ordering process felt a bit strange. The layout has two floors, and the coffee bar is right by the entrance. They make the coffee and call out numbers, but it’s easy to miss if you’re upstairs. I didn’t realize my number was called until one of the baristas waved at me. Honestly, with such a big staff, why not bring orders to customers? It feels like such a small change would make the experience a lot better.

Overall, the filter coffee I had was decent—paired well with the eclair—I recommend it ❤️

Ali Elhendi is one of the oldest and most known local coffee shops in Alexandria.

Its establishment dates back to 1882, to the time when the whole area was starting to form its current shape.

The coffee shop was owned by a Greek woman named “Maria Christo Banias” and an Egyptian man named Ali Elhendi who later purchased the entire coffee shop from Maria and has held his name since then.

The coffee shop itself is not anything special, but the place itself, the Italian architecture that surrounds the place, the vibes and history is what distinguishes Ali Elhendi from other coffee shops in the city.
